 The first respondent as
complainant filed a complaint before the District Forum against the respondents/opposite
parties praying for the direction to the opposite parties to pay a sum of Rs.12,000/-
for the instruments original costs with interest 12% interest with cost. The
District Forum allowed the complaint, against the said order, this appeal is
preferred praying to set aside the order of the District Forum dt.28.02.2007 in
C.C.85/2005.
This
appeal coming before us for hearing finally on 14.09.2010, upon hearing the
arguments of the counsels on eitherside, this commission made the following
order:
Counsel for the
Appellants /1 & 2OPs : Mr.S.K.
Chandrakumar, Advocate.
Counsel for the Respondent/Complainant : Served Absent.
Counsel for the R3 & 4/3 & 4 OPs.
: Served Absent.
M. THANIKACHALAM J,
PRESIDENT
1. The first and
second opposite parties are the appellant.
2. The complainant as
consumer, sought certain reliefs, against the opposite parties, inter alia,
contending that he had purchased a Nokia Mobile Phone Model 6600 for
Rs.12,000/- on 16.09.2005, that within 4 days, it got struck up and not
functioning, reported to the opposite parties, that though they have received the
instrument, failed to rectify the mistake or failed to replace the defective
mobile phone by new one, thereby, they committed deficiency in service, for
which, there should be direction against them, as catalogued in the prayer
column.
3. The first and second
opposite parties admitting the purchase of the mobile phone by the complainant,
denying the accusation leveled against them, would contend that on seeing the
instrument, when tendered for service, it was reported that the fault was
"Liquid Logged", which is not covered under the warranty, that the
defect was not possible to be rectified, thereby, the same was returned, which
cannot be termed as deficiency in service, thereby, praying for the dismissal
of the case, denying other averments also specifically.
4. The District Forum, by
its order dated 28.02.2007, fixing deficiency in service against the opposite
parties, directed them to pay the cost of the mobile phone, with interest
thereon with cost of Rs.3,000/-, which is challenged/impugned only by the first
and second opposite parties, as appellants.
5. Heard the learned counsel
for the appellants, perused the documents, written
submission as well as the order of the District Forum.
6. Admittedly,
and as seen from Ex.A1 also, the complainant had purchased a Nokia Mobile Phone
Model 6600 on 16.09.2005 by paying a sum
of Rs.12,000/-. As pleaded in the
complaint, which is also proved by Ex.A2, the Mobile Phone does not function
properly, hanging had taken place, for which, the instrument was handed over to
the Nokia Care Centre, under warranty, thereby indicating within the short
period, the Mobile Phone had problem, it may be manufacturing defect or otherwise. Thereafter also, once again the problem had
arisen, for which, the mobile phone was handed over to the service provider on
29.9.2005, as evidenced by Ex.A3, under warranty alone, which appears to have
been sent to the fourth opposite party for repair. Even thereafter, the problem was not
rectified, thereby, the complainant was compelled to hand over the Mobile Phone
once again for service or remove the defect on 4.10.2005, as seen from Ex.A4, this is also given under warranty. Thus, the complainant has made out a prima
facie case of purchasing a defective, unworkable Mobile Phone from the so
called reputed company of Nokia from its dealer. The Authorized Service Providers have also
failed to rectify the defects. Because
of the above proved fact, which is also supported by affidavit of the
complainant, we should conclude that there was unfair trade practice or atleast
there was deficiency in service on the part of the opposite parties. Considering all the above facts, a direction
has been issued to pay the value of the Mobile Phone with interest, in which
finding, we are unable to find any legal error, warranting our interference
legally also.
7. The learned counsel for
the appellants would contend, that the repair had occurred to the Mobile Phone
due to wetting, which could not be repaired, and for that, the complainant
alone should be held responsible, and in that case, the Mobile Phone was not
taken for service under warranty. Except
the oral submission, which has the tendency of evaporation, we do not find any
materials to preserve the same, as acceptable one. In none of Job Card given by the opposite
parties or on their behalf, it is said "Not under warranty or Liquid
Logged". Therefore, on this ground,
for the non-functioning of the Mobile Phone, we cannot hold, responsible the complainant.
8. Finally, a submission was
made on behalf of the appellants, that in case, the amount should be refunded,
the complainant should surrender the old Mobile Phone, which is not the order
of the District Forum and it should be rectified. As seen from the complaint in Para 7, it is
the specific case of the complainant, that he had handed over the old Mobile
Phone and requested the first opposite party to replace a new Mobile
Phone. Though an attempt was made, to
challenge this averment, we find no supportive evidence. In our considered opinion, the user/consumer
would not have taken back the unusable Mobile Phone and if at all, he should
have left only with the first opposite party.
In Ex.A4, taking the Mobile Phone from the complainant is admitted and
we find no indication regarding the Mobile Phone, delivery with date. Therefore, we are constrained to hold, that
the complainant should have handed over the defective Mobile Phone to the first
opposite party and this being the position, we cannot impose a condition, that
the complainant should once again surrender his old Mobile Phone in order to
receive the payment, which was also considered by the District Forum, thereby,
rendering a just and legal conclusion, to which, we subscribe our view. For the above said reasons, the appeal is
devoid of merit, liable to be dismissed.
9. In the
result, the appeal is dismissed, confirming the order passed by the District
Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum, Erode, in O.P.85/2005, dated
28.02.2007. Under the facts and
circumstances of the case, there will be no order as to cost in this appeal.
S. SAMBANDAM VASUGI
RAMANAN M.THANIKACHALAM 

 

 MEMBER II MEMBER I PRESIDENT
